Shell(cd /home/alhiefikri/telegram-bot && git commit -F - <<'EOF' fix(klikqris): make reconciliation fair and bounded without starvation Reconciliation always started from the lowest Payment id, so eligible rows that never advance (pending, outcome_unknown, recently released terminal) consumed the whole per-run cap every minute and starved newer Payments. - Replace earliest-first selection with a durable rotating keyset cursor (created_at, id) persisted per environment in the cache. Each sweep resumes after the last offered row and wraps once the whole eligible set had a turn, so a single stuck Payment no longer starves the rest. - Bound each sweep with a wall-clock execution budget (default 45s) measured on a monotonic clock, and widen the scheduler mutex to cover it so a slow provider cannot make consecutive sweeps overlap. - Add a Postgres partial index matching the cursor predicate, config defaults and env documentation, and regression tests proving newer candidates get a turn across runs, the cursor wraps after a full pass, and an exhausted execution budget stops the sweep. Recovery still reuses the same Payment, never creates a second one, and never falls back to another provider automatically. Closes #417 Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot <noreply@commandcode.ai> EOF)
